story_type: moon rocket ignition and liftoff filmed at 500 frames a second from the base of the launch tower
hook: A camera at the foot of Apollo 11 as the engines lit.
narration: This camera sat at the base of Apollo 11's launch tower as the engines lit.
It filmed at five hundred frames a second, so about thirty seconds of launch became eight minutes.
Kerosene and liquid oxygen spill out and catch fire first. That spins up the turbines that drive fuel to the F-1 engines.
At full thrust, the exhaust drags the billowing gas down under the rocket and into the flame trench.
Some three hundred thousand gallons of water poured onto the launcher to cool it and soften the shock waves.
Its surfaces were painted with a coating built to char and burn away, protecting the steel underneath.
outcome: At liftoff the hold-down arms let go, and Apollo 11 climbed away and left the launcher burning.
title: Apollo 11 engines at 500 frames a second
description:
On July 16, 1969, camera E-8 at the base of the Launch Umbilical Tower filmed the Apollo 11 Saturn V's engines at 500 frames per second, stretching about 30 seconds of launch into eight minutes.

Footage: NASA/Kennedy Space Center video, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_launch,_video_of_engines_at_500_fps_(camera_E-8).ogv

facts.claim: Camera E-8 sat at the base of the Launch Umbilical Tower and filmed at 500 frames per second, about 30 seconds of real time
facts.source_quote: Camera E-8 captured this footage on 16 mm film at 500 frames per second. This footage takes place within approximately 30 seconds of real time.

facts.claim: Initial flames are kerosene and liquid oxygen ignited, spinning up turbines that drive fuel to the F-1 engines
facts.source_quote: The initial flames are the result of kerosene and liquid oxygen being released from the Saturn V rocket's fuel tanks and being ignited by hypergolic cartridges, which spin up the turbines and drive fuel to the F-1 engines.

facts.claim: At full thrust the exhaust pulls gas below the vehicle into the flame trench
facts.source_quote: After reaching full thrust, the downward force of the exhaust creates a low pressure area which pulls the billowing gas below the vehicle and into the flame trench.

facts.claim: About 300,000 gallons of water cooled the pad and dampened shock waves; ablative coating burned off to protect surfaces
facts.source_quote: the pad's Water Deluge System discharged some 300,000 gallons of water onto the surfaces of the Mobile Launcher and Launch Umbilical Tower

facts.claim: At T-0 the hold-down arms release the rocket
facts.source_quote: At T-0, the hold down arms release the rocket
